svg.text: Azure GPU VM stack: layers and where compatibility matters
ND / NC (passthrough) and NV (vGPU) SKUs on Azure, from the AKS / HPC image point of view
GUEST VM = THE IMAGE (HPC image / AKS VHD): image builder controls
⑤ Physical host firmware: CRD bundle
CRD = versioned hardware + firmware bundle per SKU; it lists the recommended / highest validated guest GPU driver.
Updated by the fleet independently of the guest image; mixed CRDs coexist in the fleet during rollouts.
FLEET / PLATFORM: image cannot choose; a VM lands on whatever CRD the host runs
Crosses the image ↔ fleet boundary: image team controls only one side
Inside the image: fully controlled by version pinning at build time
Passthrough: the guest driver talks to the GPU directly. Each CRD
lists a recommended / max validated driver; newer drivers are usually
backward compatible but not guaranteed on every older CRD. New GPUs
Symptom: Driver fails to load, Xid errors, GPU missing / off the bus
Cross-node NVLink depends on the switch-tray firmware in the rack
CRD plus the IMEX / driver version in the guest.
Symptom: Compute domain fails to form; NVLink down
Guest GRID driver ↔ host vGPU manager
Guest GRID branch must be supported by the host vGPU manager.
The one host/guest issue AKS has seen (A10).
Symptom: No vGPU, licensing errors, nvidia-smi fails
Driver and NIC firmware must be in NVIDIA Networking's supported
matrix; the NIC firmware ships with the CRD.
Symptom: IB link flaps, RDMA errors, NCCL bandwidth drops
Exact version match with the driver (e.g. 580.159.04 = 580.159.04).
Symptom: FM fails to start, CUDA init fails, no NVLink
nvidia.ko, amdgpu and OFED modules must be built for the running
kernel (DKMS at build, or prebaked per kernel).
Symptom: Module missing after a kernel update
Driver's CUDA version must be ≥ CUDA runtime in the image / containers.
Device plugin / DRA, dcgm-exporter and container toolkit must match
the driver, DCGM and containerd versions. AKS stays source of truth.
Symptom: GPUs not advertised to kubelet, metrics missing
• The image fixes everything above the hypervisor; the fleet fixes everything below.
• A, C, D and E are the only places host firmware and the image meet. Mitigation: pin
drivers to versions validated across the CRDs live in the fleet for each SKU.
• B, F, G and H are solved at build time by version pinning + build validation.
• AMD (MI300X) follows the same pattern: amdgpu (DKMS) + ROCm in the image,
amdgpu ↔ GPU firmware (PSP / IFWI) in the CRD.
